MTP k=2 on this row (2026-10-19): ITL 22.2 -> 19.8 ms, real-text decode unchanged (110.7 vs 112.0 tok/s); k=3 kept. The c1 decode gap is the serial four-stage step (stage 3 carries MTP and lm_head), not tuning.

notes: Named alternative (chosen 2026-10-25): automatic selection keeps fn-quad-3090-nop2p (TP2xPP2+EP) as the no-P2P default; this row runs only when named: merlin serve flash-next <dir> --profile fn-quad-3090-nop2p-pp4, or bash tools/merlin/launchers/serve-quad-3090-nop2p-pp4.sh <dir>.

Pick it for long prefills: no tensor-parallel all-reduce, so 32K-262K prompts prefill ~1.5x faster than the TP2xPP2 row without P2P; c1 decode is 14 % slower (four stages run in series at one request).

Measured pool 906,581 tokens (3 x 262K / 6 x 131K resident fit) at pin 4,456,448,000 bytes (250 whole stage-3 blocks) with partition 12/13/13/10 and max_num_seqs=32; the earlier 2,500,000,000-byte pin gave 506,083 tokens. The even 12/12/12/12 partition OOMed on stage 3.
No --enable-expert-parallel (EP is a no-op at TP1; whether the tree boots with the flag at TP1 is unverified).
NCCL_PROTO is left to NCCL: the earlier LL default has never been compared with NCCL's own choice without P2P.
Cold-start risk on host-staged PP relays: DUFRelic batches the three tensor-dict isend/irecv call sites with batch_isend_irecv; that patch is not in this tree.
profiles.acceptance: Tested on the reference host with P2P off (pool, decode at 4K / 131K / 262K, needles, 8 MP smoke). Still open: token identity against a P2P control and a physical no-P2P host. TP2xPP2 stays the no-P2P default.

profiles.title: 8 x RTX 3090 24 GB, TP2xPP4+EP, max-num-seqs 32 (octo default; P2P on or off)

capacity.basis: Estimate from the engine's own get_kv_cache_configs evaluated on per-stage specs (v3.0.0 tree); the TP2xPP2 25/23 calibration at 4.1e9 reproduces 924,993 tokens exactly. Pin = card VRAM - binding-stage weights - 2.75 GiB overhead; the weights are derived except TP2xPP2 (measured). An ESTIMATE until a pool-only boot on the hardware.

evidence: Community: brandon-nuttall, halt95/qwen38-flash-next-3090s pull request (2026-10-03, v2.2.0 image): 7x RTX 3090 + 1x 3090 Ti, TP2xPP4, VLLM_PP_LAYER_PARTITION=12,12,12,12, --kv-cache-memory 9e9, gmu 0.93, seqs 8, MTP K=3: 8-way aggregate 268-312 tok/s (325-346 with greedy draft + local argmax).

Community: Jon-Nielsen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Merlin-3090-Serving-Kit v2 (HF, 2026-09-16): 8x RTX 3090 at 180 W, PCIe only, P2P blocked by BAR1 VBIOS, TP4xPP2+EP, MTP-4, BF16 KV, max_num_seqs 32: pool 1,317,519 at 262K, 131.0 tok/s single stream, ~239 tok/s 4-stream aggregate. Older stack (wtdcode vllm-backport v0.13), not this engine.
notes: Default octo layout and concurrency: TP2xPP4+EP with --max-num-seqs 32; the quad stays at 8.

Why PP4: the model has 2 KV heads, so TP4 duplicates them (one per rank, as at TP2); splitting by PP halves the layers per card instead. At equal pins TP2xPP4 holds 4.88M tokens against 2.87M for TP4xPP2.

Partition 12,12,12,12 is the basis of the capacity estimates and of brandon-nuttall's rig. The last stage binds (lm_head + MTP + the extra QSA layer: 9.0 against 6.8 MiB per block); 13/12/12/11 and 13/13/12/10 are candidate alternatives, and the choice stays open.

KV pin 11.25 GiB: pool 4,656,696 tokens, 17 x 262K, 31 x 131K resident. max-num-seqs stays 32 as the admission cap, so the stated fit is 31 x 131K. The 11.55 GiB sizing estimate (4,780,487 tokens, 32 x 131K) is the paper alternative: the 2.75 GiB overhead line was measured at seqs 8, and 32 seqs add larger graphs and sampler buffers (budget +0.3 to +0.6 GiB, unmeasured). 10.95 GiB gives 4,529,265 tokens / 30 x 131K. If the boot refuses the pin, lower KV_BYTES one step; if it passes with headroom, 11.55 is worth trying. KV_BYTES is a per-card pin estimate: after a pool-only boot read the logged pool and adjust in 0.25 GiB steps (lower it if the boot OOMs).
Graph capture sizes extend to 128 decode tokens (32 x (K+1)).

PP>2 path check: a TP1xPP4 run (seqs 32, MTP K=3) on four 3090s on a pre-release vLLM 0.32 build booted in 227 s with a 506,083-token pool, and the smoke and pipeline-tail checks passed. That exercised the PP>2 code path (MTP and RecoverSSM at pp=4 with 32 sequences) on the quad. It is a four-card stand-in, not an eight-card memory budget: no eight-card run exists, so this TP2xPP4 shape, its 12,12,12,12 partition and its pin are unvalidated.

Fallback if the first octo boot fails on the last stage: on the quad TP1xPP4 the stock 12,12,12,12 OOMed on stage 3, the last stage (lm_head + MTP + the extra QSA layer, the stage that binds here too), and the measured partition there is 12,13,13,10 at a 2.5e9 pin. Try a 12,13,13,10-style split (13/13/12/10 is already listed above) or a lower pin (10.95 GiB) first, and report which one booted.

GPU order: with CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0..7 the TP pairs are (0,1) (2,3) (4,5) (6,7) and the PP edges run pair to pair; list the cards so each TP pair shares the best link. models/flash-next/topo_select.py handles four GPUs only.
Host RAM: 69 GiB floor / 96 GB qualified were measured with four workers; eight workers add roughly 8 GiB (estimate from ~8 GiB across four workers and the engine).

P2P=on (default) uses the qualified 4-card settings (brandon-nuttall's report does not say whether his rig had P2P). P2P=off uses Jon-Nielsen's NCCL settings (NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1, ring algorithm, LL128, --disable-custom-all-reduce), the only 8-card evidence without peer-to-peer (his rig ran TP4xPP2 on an older stack, so TP2xPP4 without P2P is untested on any stack).

Optional community knob, not in this profile: greedy draft + use_local_argmax_reduction gave +10-20 % 8-way aggregate and -8 to -10 % single-stream at 4K on brandon's rig; it changes the draft sampling mode, so it needs its own qualification.
profiles.acceptance: A community 8 x 3090 run on Merlin 3.x reporting pool, decode at 4K/131K/262K, needles and the smoke test. The PP>2 path check (TP1xPP4 on a four-card 3090 host) is done and is not an eight-card result.
